questions.q: What is the real risk of hardcoding a credential directly in notebook code?
options: The credential now exists in the notebook's revision history, on any screen viewing that cell, and in any copy of the code
Databricks clusters cannot run notebooks that contain any string values
It has no real risk as long as the notebook is never shared
Hardcoded credentials are automatically encrypted by Databricks
questions.explain: A hardcoded value persists everywhere the notebook's text is stored, viewed, or copied — not just in the moment it's typed.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a Databricks-backed and an Azure Key Vault-backed secret scope?
options: A Key Vault-backed scope stores the value in Key Vault, governed by Key Vault's own policies; a Databricks-backed scope stores it in Databricks-managed storage
A Key Vault-backed scope is always slower to read from than a Databricks-backed scope
Databricks-backed scopes cannot be used with dbutils.secrets.get()
There is no functional difference between the two scope types
questions.explain: Where the value actually lives determines which system's access policies, rotation, and audit trail govern it.

questions.q: Why would an organization choose a Key Vault-backed secret scope over a Databricks-backed one?
options: When the secret already has to be managed by an existing enterprise process (rotation, access reviews) that lives in Key Vault, so it's governed once instead of duplicated
Key Vault-backed scopes are required for every Databricks cluster regardless of use case
Databricks-backed scopes cannot store passwords, only API keys
Key Vault-backed scopes remove the need to call dbutils.secrets.get()
questions.explain: Pointing Databricks at an existing Key Vault avoids maintaining the same secret's policy in two separate systems.

questions.q: What happens if a notebook accidentally prints a value retrieved via dbutils.secrets.get()?
options: Databricks automatically redacts the known secret value in the notebook's output
The cluster immediately terminates to prevent exposure
The secret scope is automatically deleted
Nothing — Databricks has no protection against this at all
questions.explain: Redaction is a safety net against accidental exposure in output — it doesn't replace keeping the value out of the code text itself.

questions.q: When creating a Key Vault-backed secret scope, what does Databricks actually store?
options: A reference to the vault (its DNS name and resource ID), not a copy of any secret value
A plaintext copy of every secret in the vault
An encrypted duplicate of the vault's entire contents
Nothing is stored — the scope has no persistent configuration at all
questions.explain: The reference lets Databricks read secrets from Key Vault at request time, without ever holding its own copy of the value.
